Subject: Science
Hook: Why you feel colder in water than in air at the same temperature.
Caption:
Why you feel colder in water than in air at the same temperature.

20°C air feels mild. 20°C water feels freezing. The temperature is identical — what changes is the rate.

Water conducts heat away from your skin roughly 25 times faster than air, so your body loses warmth far quicker even though the water isn't colder.

This is the difference between temperature and heat transfer, and it's the single idea most Grade 8 students never quite separate.

Save this for exam week.

Debugging is a method, not a mood.
Most kids debug by staring harder and changing things at random.

Hook: Squaring any number ending in 5, in two seconds.
Caption:
Squaring any number ending in 5, in two seconds.

Take the digits before the 5. Multiply by the next number up. Stick 25 on the end.

35² → 3 × 4 = 12 → 1225.
65² → 6 × 7 = 42 → 4225.
95² → 9 × 10 = 90 → 9025.
125² → 12 × 13 = 156 → 15625.

It works for every single one, and the algebra behind it is one line of expansion — which makes it a nice bridge into why identities are useful at all.

Students panic at unseen passages because they treat them as a comprehension test. They're a technique test, and technique can be prepared even when the text can't.

The unseen text question.
You can't prepare the text. You can prepare the technique.
1. READ THE QUESTION FIRST. Then the passage. Never the other way round.
2. ANNOTATE FOR THE QUESTION ONLY. Ignore everything else, however interesting.
3. FIND THREE MOMENTS, spread across the passage. Beginning, middle, end.
4. FOR EACH: what the writer does, then WHY it works on a reader.
5. The 'why it works on a reader' is where almost all the marks live.
Most students describe the technique and stop. That's half a mark of a possible three.
Prepare the shape. The text takes care of itself.
